Conduct weekly visual scouting for wilt symptoms (Fusarium, Verticillium) and pest presence (aphids, bollworms); apply appropriate fungicides or insecticides if thresholds are exceeded.

steps.consensus: Soil pH and texture are well-suited for cotton, and current weather temperature/humidity are within ideal bounds, but the crop is suffering from critical moisture deficit and low canopy vigor that threatens yield.

Low organic carbon in soil combined with high soil exposure increasing erosion and nutrient loss risks

merged_opportunities: Favorable ambient temperature, humidity, and soil pH provide good base conditions once moisture is restored
Early satellite detection of canopy stress allows immediate corrective actions like flood/drip irrigation and mulching
High nitrogen and suitable soil texture support rapid recovery if organic carbon and water management are addressed

conflicts.description: WeatherAgent reports excellent ambient conditions, whereas SatelliteAgent indicates critical vegetation health and severe water stress.
conflicts.resolution: Prioritize SatelliteAgent ground observation of crop stress; immediate irrigation is required despite mild ambient weather.

conflicts.description: SoilAgent reports a high soil health score of 90 with optimal pH and nitrogen, contrasting with SatelliteAgent findings of high bare soil exposure and critical canopy health.
conflicts.resolution: Recognize that favorable soil chemistry does not compensate for immediate water deficits; focus on moisture retention and soil organic carbon enhancement.

steps.finding: Implement immediate flood irrigation to alleviate critical water stress and apply organic compost/manure to raise soil organic carbon.
actions: Activate flood irrigation today, delivering enough water to bring soil moisture to field capacity and maintain it every 7‑10 days during the flowering stage.
Apply 5‑7 tons/ha of well‑decomposed compost or organic manure across the field within the next 3‑5 days, incorporating it lightly into the top 15 cm.
Install temporary mulch (straw or plastic mulch) over the rows to reduce evaporation and protect soil surface.
Set up soil moisture sensors (tensiometers or capacitance probes) at representative points and record readings daily.
Conduct weekly visual scouting for wilt symptoms (Fusarium, Verticillium) and pest presence (aphids, bollworms); apply appropriate fungicides or insecticides if thresholds are exceeded.
steps.justification: Satellite imagery shows critical vegetation health and severe moisture deficit, while soil analysis indicates low organic carbon. Immediate water supply will restore canopy vigor, and organic amendments will improve soil structure, nutrient retention, and reduce disease/pest susceptibility, leveraging the already optimal temperature, humidity, pH, and nitrogen levels.
steps.influence: Translated the executive decision into concrete recommended actions.
